topic: A neighbor wants to install a fence
text: I remember when the skies were woven into the fabric of our yard, the clouds drifting as freely as the dandelions. Now, Mr. Thompson speaks of fences, as if to contain the very breeze. Part of me wants to ask why we must draw lines where there were none, why we must alter the landscape that has cradled our memories. Yet, I find myself nodding, agreeing to discussions and arrangements, as if the solidifying of boundaries could somehow make everything clearer. But I can't shake the whisper of a past where no fences were needed, where the world seemed larger and more connected. I suppose, in a way, this fence is a promise to respect his space, but it feels like I'm losing something I never realized I cherished.
